correctness.rationale: For n>=4k,k>=2 and 1<ik/n<=2, crossing the mean means event H>=2. Monotone marked-set coupling and adding unmarked population reduce to (n,i)=(rk-1,r), r=floor(n/k)+1>=5. The order-five integer Bonferroni minorant L5(h)=sum_{j=2}^5(-1)^j(j-1)C(h,j) is <=1_{h>=2} at every integer h; factorial moments give B5. k=2,3,4 have displayed strictly positive rational 4P-1. For k,r>=5, independently expanded Q=120(N)_5(B5-1/4), N=rk-1, in x=r-5,y=k-5, and reproduced the complete 6x6 positive-coefficient matrix (minimum coefficient 1, constant 12528000). Degree <=5 in each variable plus exact 6x6 interpolation is a polynomial identity, not merely finite enumeration; every nonnegative x,y yields Q>0. Sequence k=2,n=2i-1 yields P=i/[2(2i-1)] -> 1/4.
residual_risks: The proof depends on an exact fifth-degree polynomial identity; independently expanded coefficients, but no independent formal verification.
